source_note: Both native binaries include the same preexisting local SVG changes, which are excluded from this commit. The baseline is the published round-six final binary. The baseline XCTest bundle and unchanged workload source match the previous recorded hashes.

fixed_work_comparison.method: Two prebuilt renderer XCTest bundles, 120 tracks and 60 completed mutation states per mode. Separate serial processes use identical optimization settings. One state in flight; document and scroll tile completion checked. Applied state and installed-tree pixel checks run outside measured intervals. Process CPU includes worker threads. Elapsed time includes completion barriers. Work equality requires identical completed state, layout, document job, document install, scroll raster, tile job and compositor raster counts across all rounds of each mode. Renderer callbacks are not treated as completed frames. This is a renderer-component comparison, not WebKit, full-host throughput or display FPS. The checkout workload source and both bundle executable hashes must remain unchanged throughout the comparison; callers must build both bundles from the same workload source.
fixed_work_comparison.order: Before then after in round 1; reversed in alternate rounds

comparison.method: Serial baseline and optimized native binaries plus WebKit; reverse order in round two. Both native binaries enable the published scroll batching and obsolete-raster cancellation. Both retain canonical resolved paint exclusion caching. Selected additionally fuses exclusion predicates into one traversal and avoids subtree backdrop scans when the document has no backdrop filters. Experimental scroll-owned takeover is disabled. Transport recording disabled. CPU is percent of one core, including WebKit helpers, excluding WindowServer. Host callbacks are not display FPS.
comparison.work_count_note: Native-only tile work is measured over the CPU measurement interval, normalized by sandbox callbacks; these are not display frames. Layout counts include the entire capture, including startup and warmup. Different free-running work counts prevent treating CPU percentage as cost per equal completed state.
comparison.host_execution_note: Capture uses the standalone harness default executor; manual native checks separately use --background to exercise the production detached executor. This is not a full Telegram app benchmark.

new_fixture.name: nested-clips
new_fixture.changes: Fractional placement, nested widths, track translation, text readings and stacking order; no renderer-specific code or sandbox quota changes.

manual.method: Manual CUA interactions in separate native and WebKit standalone previews, one running at a time. Native uses --background. Functional states and clipping were inspected; this is not a presented-frame trace or proof of hitch-free animation.

remaining_limits: Fixed-work medians are incremental and their run ranges overlap; they do not establish a uniform improvement.
Free-running callback counts are not display FPS and do not hold completed paint work constant.
Only macOS integration was measured. The matcher is portable C++ with standalone tests; other platform performance was not measured.
Offscreen paint deferral remains unimplemented. Fresh first exposure requires coordination with host scrolling.
No universal speedup, 2x advantage over WebKit, or hitch-free 60 FPS result is established.
